---
title: "Sound 2: Oscillators and Pulse-Width Modulation"
toc: true
toc-depth: 2
---

An **oscillator** is the part of a synthesizer that makes a repeating wave. Its two settings are
the **shape** of the wave and how fast it repeats (the **frequency**, heard as pitch). This lesson
plays the classic shapes from [the harmonic series lesson](sound-harmonics.qmd) on a real
oscillator, then makes the pulse wave move.

**How to use the page.** Press ▶, or play the computer keys (`a w s e d…`), the on-screen keyboard
or a MIDI keyboard; the widget sounds while a key is held. Keep the volume in the bottom bar low to
start with. The bright waves are loud.

## Four shapes

<div class="sk" data-w="wave" data-set="type=sine"></div>

Play the same note with each **Wave** and watch both pictures:

- **Sine**: one spike in the spectrum.
- **Triangle**: a few odd harmonics that die away fast. Softer than you'd guess from the pointed shape.
- **Sawtooth**: a comb of every harmonic. The brightest and the most useful, because a filter can
  carve almost anything out of it.
- **Square**: only every other spike. Listen for the hollow, woody tone.

Move **Pitch** up and down. On the spectrum the whole comb slides along together, keeping its
pattern. That pattern (the timbre) is independent of the pitch.

::: {.sk-tip}
**Frequency and pitch.** Each octave doubles the frequency: A2 is 110 Hz, A3 220 Hz, A4 440 Hz.
That's why the spectrum's frequency axis is drawn with every octave the same width.
:::

## Pulse width

A pulse wave is up for part of each cycle and down for the rest. The fraction of the cycle it
spends up is the **pulse width** (or *duty cycle*). At 50% it is a square wave.

<div class="sk" data-w="wave" data-set="type=pulse,width=0.5" data-title="Pulse width"></div>

Drag **Pulse width** slowly from 50% down to 5%. The sound goes from hollow to nasal to thin and
reedy. On the spectrum, gaps appear and move: at width 1/*k*, every *k*th harmonic is missing.
Widths of 30% and 70% sound the same: one is the other upside down.

Inside the browser there is no pulse oscillator, so the widget makes one the way some analogue
synths did: it takes a sawtooth and subtracts a delayed copy of the same sawtooth. The delay, as a
fraction of the cycle, is the pulse width.

## PWM: pulse-width modulation

Now let something move the width for you. **PWM rate** is how many times a second the width swings,
and **PWM depth** is how far.

<div class="sk" data-w="wave" data-set="type=pulse,width=0.5,pwmDepth=0.35,pwmRate=0.6,freq=110" data-title="PWM"></div>

A slowly swinging pulse width gives the rich, chorus-like shimmer of 1980s string machines and
synth pads: the gaps in the spectrum sweep up and down, a little like a [phaser](sound-phaser.qmd).
Turn the rate up to 5 Hz or so for a wobble. The thing doing the moving is an **LFO**, a low-frequency
oscillator, which gets [its own lesson](sound-lfo.qmd).
